decisions.quote: As far as solution-focused questions are concerned, it seems logical that they decreased negative affect, but it is puzzling that they did not produce a statistically significant effect on positive affect, as they did in Grant´s ( 2012) study.
decisions.reason: The authors confirm Grant's (2012) findings for four of the five tested variables (negative affect, self-efficacy, goal approach, and action steps), framing this as holding for 'the majority of the variables we studied' rather than giving an unqualified overall verdict on the replication as a whole. Because they explicitly contrast the absence of a statistically significant effect on positive affect in the solution-focused condition with Grant's (2012) result, the outcome is mixed.
